Top candidates: **Common_smut** (galls on leaves, white/gray when young) or possibly **Common_rust** (pustules). Let me check references.

Common_rust doesn't match (brick-red pustules). Common_smut shows larger galls. The test image has tiny fleshy white/yellow raised galls on a leaf. Let me check Head_smut and also Tar_spot/Physoderma for comparison.

Head_smut shows black spore masses in ears/tassels — doesn't match. Physoderma shows banding/spots — doesn't match. The test image clearly shows raised, fleshy, white-yellow galls on a leaf. Let me check a couple more to confirm Common_smut vs other candidates.

Tar_spot shows small black tar-like spots — not raised fleshy galls. Anthracnose shows brown lesions with dark margins — very different.

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: Multiple raised, fleshy, white-to-yellowish gall structures on a corn leaf blade
- These are clearly not flat lesions, pustules, or spots — they are 3D fleshy growths
- **Common_smut** matches perfectly: "Galls initially white to gray and fleshy... can appear on any above-ground plant part including leaves"
- The galls haven't yet turned black (still in early white/yellowish stage)
- Head_smut only affects tassels/ears with spore masses — doesn't match
- All other candidates produce flat lesions, pustules, or spots — none match raised fleshy galls
